item.title: FDA Clinical Decision Support Software Guidance Refresh- Clearer Rules, Broader Innovation
item.description: On January 6, 2026, the FDA issued a Guidance for Industry and Food and Drug Administration Staff regarding Clinical Decision Support (CDS) software. The January 2026 guidance supersedes the previous, and less detailed, guidance document on the topic issued on September 28, 2022. item.title: Navigating the AI Employment Landscape in 2026- Considerations and Best Practices for Employers
item.description: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) regulation and litigation are set to take center stage in 2026, as both federal and state governments introduce new laws, guidance, and enforcement priorities. This year employers will face a rapidly evolving patchwork of state-level AI governance statutes, including landmark laws in Colorado, California, Illinois, Texas, and New Jersey, each imposing distinct requirements for transparency, risk assessment, and anti-discrimination in the use of AI system

item.title: The Importance of Internal Wage and Hour Audits
item.description: Wage and hour class and collective action claims remain some of the most common employment claims. In a regulatory environment where the federal Department of Labor (DOL) is operating with diminished resources, it is likely that private litigation in the wage and hour space will continue to rise. As employers who have faced these types of claims know, once litigation is filed, the cost of wage and hour mistakes adds up quickly, given the imposition of liquidated damages and attorneys’ fee awards

item.title: Recruiting and Hiring Without Stepping on Legal Landmines
item.description: Hiring a new employee should be exciting. It means growth, new ideas, and added capacity. But from a legal and financial perspective, hiring is also one of the riskiest things a business does. Every decision, from how a job is posted to what questions are asked in an interview, can have legal consequences if handled carelessly. item.title: Some Useful Tips for Avoiding and Addressing Employment Retaliation Claims
item.description: Retaliation is one of the most commonly alleged employment-related claims, often asserted in conjunction with other discrimination claims, and can be more challenging to address and defend than the underlying discrimination claim.
